book: Mermaid Roshan and the Dust Bunnies

rules.exact: Every v45_text and v45_bubbles string must appear exactly: same words, spelling, capitals and punctuation, with curly quotes and apostrophes and three plain periods for ellipses.
rules.line_breaks: A newline marks a line or pause break. Lines may be re-wrapped to fit the caption box; no words may be cut.
rules.unchanged: Pages with changed=false keep their V44 text and caption placement byte for byte. The rear cover text is unchanged.

rear_text:
Pearl Castle needs help.
Where will Roshan begin?

pages.v44_text:
“Look, Daddy!
Pearl Castle!”
pages.v45_text:
“Look, Daddy!
Pearl Castle!”

pages.v44_text:
The plane landed at Sky Lagoon.
Pearl Castle was close by.
pages.v45_text:
The plane landed at Sky Lagoon.
Pearl Castle was close by.

pages.v44_text:
“Let’s look inside,
Daddy,” said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
“Let’s look inside,
Daddy,” said Roshan.

pages.v44_text:
Inside, dust covered the floor.
“Let’s clean it together!”
said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
Inside, dust covered the floor.
“It’s SO messy!” said Roshan.
“Where do we start?”
pages.why: Gives Roshan a feeling every child knows, a mess that looks too big, and sets up Daddy's answer and the big-job lesson.

pages.v44_text:
Sniff, sniff!
Someone was sniffling behind a big shell door.
“Hello?” said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
Sniff, sniff!
Someone was sniffling behind a big shell door.
“Hello?” said Roshan. But the door was stuck.
“We’ll come back!” she promised.
pages.why: She no longer walks away from someone in need: the door is stuck and she promises to come back (your choice).

pages.v44_text:
Daddy gave her a brush and some sponges.
“One little job at a time,” said Daddy.
pages.v45_text:
Daddy gave her a duster and two sponges.
“One little job at a time,” said Daddy.
pages.why: The picture shows a feather duster and two sponges; the words now name them exactly.

pages.v44_text:
A dust bunny splashed in the dirty bath.
It loved to play. Splash, splash!
pages.v45_text:
A dust bunny splashed in the dirty bath.
Splash, splash! Gunk went everywhere!
The little bunny just wanted to play.
pages.why: The bunny's play causes trouble, but it just wants to play: the first of three "just" moments.

pages.v44_text:
Round and round went the sponge.
Roshan wiped the sink clean.
pages.v45_text:
Roshan started with one little job: the sink.
Round and round went her sponge!
pages.why: Roshan answers her own question by choosing one little job.

pages.v44_text:
Out went the dirty bath water.
Roshan scrubbed the tub. Scrub, scrub!
pages.v45_text:
The dust bunny hopped out, and Roshan pulled the plug.
Out went the dirty water!
She scrubbed the tub. Scrub, scrub!
pages.why: The bunny hops out before the plug is pulled, so no child worries it went down the drain; matches the plug-chain picture.

pages.v44_text:
Clean water filled the bath.
The dust bunny was ready to play!
pages.v45_text:
Soon the bath was sparkling clean.
Now the dust bunny had a good place to play!
Far away, someone went sniff, sniff.
pages.why: Cleaning meets the bunny's need, "sparkling" plants the sparkles of page 23, and a sniffle keeps the mystery alive.

pages.v44_text:
Rumi was stuck under the gunk.
She needed help!
pages.v45_text:
In the pool, a mermaid named Rumi was stuck under the gunk.
“Can you help me?” she called.
pages.why: Introduces Rumi and the pool, and Rumi asks for help in her own words, the words Roshan uses on page 25.

pages.v44_text:
“I’ll help!” said Roshan.
Scoop, scoop!
pages.v45_text:
“I’ll help!” said Roshan.
Scoop, scoop!

pages.v44_text:
Rainbow colors
peeked through the gunk.
pages.v45_text:
Rainbow colors
peeked through the gunk.

pages.v44_text:
Whoosh! The waterfall turned rainbow!
The swimming pool was magic!
It made the water rainbow-colored.
pages.v45_text:
Whoosh! The waterfall turned rainbow!
The pool was magic.
Its rainbow had been hiding under the gunk!
pages.why: Explains the magic simply and plants "hiding under the gunk", which returns with Grand Puff.

pages.v44_text:
A cup was stuck in the fountain.
Roshan pulled it free. Whoosh!
pages.v45_text:
A cup was stuck in the seahorse fountain.
Roshan pulled and pulled...
Out came the cup, and out came the water!
pages.why: Replaces a second "Whoosh!" with effort (pulled and pulled) and a clear cause: cup out, water out.

pages.v44_text:
The gunk was gone. Up came Rumi!
She had lived in Pearl Castle for hundreds of years.
Now she was free!
pages.v45_text:
The gunk washed away. Up came Rumi!
She had lived in Pearl Castle for hundreds of years.
Now she was free!
pages.why: Says why the gunk left: the water washed it away.

pages.v44_text:
“You helped me!”
said Rumi.
She gave Roshan
a great big hug.
pages.v45_text:
“You helped me!” said Rumi.
She gave Roshan a great big hug.
“If you ever need help, just call!”
pages.why: Rumi offers help in return, so her coming back on page 26 is earned.

pages.v44_text:
Chirp, chirp!
“Someone in the playroom
needs help!” said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
Chirp, chirp!
A worried little chirp came from the playroom.
“Someone needs help!” said Roshan.
pages.why: Names the feeling (worried) and shows how Roshan knows someone needs help.

pages.v44_text:
Two dust bunnies sat on Baby Eagle.
They wanted to play, but he was stuck.
“I’ll help!” said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
Two dust bunnies sat on Baby Eagle.
They just wanted to play, but he was stuck!
“I’ll help!” said Roshan.
pages.why: "Just wanted to play" repeats the bunnies' pattern: trouble, but not bad.

pages.v44_text:
She gently brushed one bunny away,
then the other.
pages.v45_text:
She gently brushed one bunny away,
then the other.

pages.v44_text:
Baby Eagle was free!
“Let’s play gently,” said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
Baby Eagle was free!
“Chirp, chirp!” he said happily.
“Let’s all play gently,” said Roshan.
pages.why: Your choice: an apology plus a promise; Baby Eagle forgives with a happy chirp, and everyone plays gently.

pages.v44_text:
In the art room, Roshan put
the paints in their places.
Then she scrubbed the table. Scrub, scrub!
pages.v45_text:
In the art room, Roshan put the paints in their places.
She scrubbed the table. Scrub, scrub!
“One little job at a time,” she sang.
pages.why: Roshan now says Daddy's advice herself, showing she has learned it.

pages.v44_text:
Only the big shell door was still shut.
Behind it, someone sneezed... AH-CHOO!
pages.v45_text:
Sparkles flew from every clean room to the big shell door. Click!
Roshan kept her promise.
Behind the door, someone sneezed... AH-CHOO!
pages.why: The sparkles already drawn on the page unstick the door, and she keeps her promise.

pages.v44_text:
Grand Puff!
He was covered in dust.
He did not feel well.
pages.v45_text:
It was Grand Puff, the biggest dust bunny of all!
Every sneeze puffed out more dust.
He did not feel well.
pages.why: Answers the mystery and the title: Grand Puff is the biggest dust bunny, and his sneezes cause the dust.

pages.v44_text:
“Hold on, we’ll make you feel
clean and better!” said Roshan.
pages.v45_text:
Roshan wasn’t mad. “I’ll help!” she said.
But Grand Puff was too big to wash alone.
“Can you help me?” she called.
pages.why: The heart of the lesson: she isn't mad at the one who made the mess, and the job is too big alone, so she asks for help.

pages.v44_text:
Daddy, Rumi, and Baby Eagle helped Roshan.
Together, they washed Grand Puff. Scrub, scrub!
pages.v45_text:
“We’ll help!” said Daddy and Rumi.
“Chirp, chirp!” said Baby Eagle.
Together, they washed Grand Puff. Scrub, scrub!
pages.why: The friends she helped answer "We'll help!", and Baby Eagle helps in his own voice.

pages.v44_text:
Soft bubbles covered Grand Puff.
Little colors began to shine beneath them.
pages.v45_text:
Soft bubbles covered Grand Puff.
Then rainbow colors peeked through the bubbles!
pages.why: Echoes page 13: colors peek through the bubbles the way they peeked through the gunk.

pages.v44_text:
POP! Grand Puff sprang out, rainbow bright!
The dust fell away.
pages.v45_text:
POP! Grand Puff sprang out, rainbow bright!
The dust fell away.

pages.v44_text:
Down came Grand Puff, soft and small.
He felt like himself again.
pages.v45_text:
Down came Grand Puff, soft and small.
“I feel all better!” he said.
pages.why: Grand Puff says how he feels in his own words instead of an idiom.

pages.v44_text:
The art room was tidy.
One little job at a time,
Pearl Castle was clean again.
pages.v45_text:
The art room was tidy.
Pearl Castle was clean again!
It was a big job, but friends can do big jobs together!
pages.why: Keeps the art room named and says the friendship half of the moral out loud, last on the page.

pages.v44_text:
“We helped your rainbow shine!” said Roshan.
“Thank you!” said Grand Puff.
Roshan smiled. “Come and rest with us!”
pages.v45_text:
“Sorry about all the dust,” said Grand Puff.
“That’s okay,” said Roshan.
“You just needed help. Everyone needs help sometimes!”
pages.why: Says the other half: he says sorry, and Roshan forgives him because everyone needs help sometimes. Drops the praise for his new colors.

pages.v44_text:
There was room for everyone.
They curled up and fell asleep.
pages.v45_text:
“Come and rest with us!” said Roshan.
There was room for everyone, even the dust bunnies.
They curled up together and fell asleep.
pages.why: The invitation leads straight into the nap, and "even the dust bunnies" ties the title to belonging.
